cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, and he calls them his brothers (James 1:1). He just told them pure religion means caring for orphans and widows in their distress (James 1:27). Now he's got something to say about how they treat people as they hold out their faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: As they hold out their faith in the glorious Lord Jesus Christ, what does James tell his brothers not to do?

cards.text: James paints a picture: a man wearing a gold ring and fine clothes walks into the meeting, and so does a poor man in shabby clothes. Friend, I spent YEARS under the dust in a junk drawer, so I know EXACTLY which one of those two guys I'd be.

cards.question: In James's picture, they lavish attention on the man in fine clothes. Where do they tell him to sit?
True or false: In James's picture, the poor man in shabby clothes gets offered a seat of honor too.
James asks: treating the two men that way, haven't you discriminated among yourselves and become ___ with evil thoughts?

cards.text: Then James says, "Listen, my beloved brothers:" and he turns their eyes to the poor of this world. He wants them to think about who God has chosen.

cards.question: James asks: hasn't God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in ___ and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?

cards.text: James doesn't let up: "But you have dishonored the poor." Then he asks them to think about who's REALLY been giving them trouble.

cards.question: James asks the believers who it is that oppresses them and drags them into court. Who does he name?

cards.text: And James asks: aren't they the ones who blaspheme the noble name you've been called by? Friend, that's like saving the best seat at your party for the guy who keeps keying your car.

cards.question: James points them to the royal law stated in Scripture and says if they really fulfill it, they're doing well. What does the royal law say?

answers.text: Give to the one who asks you

cards.question: True or false: James says that if they show favoritism, they sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.

cards.text: Then James takes it even further. Picture somebody who keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point.

cards.question: True or false: James says the person who keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is only guilty of that one point.

cards.text: He gives an example: He who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." Keeping one and breaking the other is like telling the officer, "But I used my BLINKER!" while doing ninety down the highway.

cards.question: James says if you don't commit adultery but do commit murder, you have become a ___.

cards.text: So James tells them how to live: speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom. Every word, every move. Whew.

cards.question: James says judgment without mercy will be shown to who?

answers.text: Anyone who has not been merciful
Anyone who has not kept the Sabbath
Anyone who has not given to the poor

cards.question: James wraps it up with one short line: ___ triumphs over judgment.

findings.problem: The card says James calls his readers his brothers and cites James 1:1 for it. James 1:1 only names James and greets the twelve tribes of the Dispersion. 'My brothers' first appears in James 1:2, and it also appears in James 2:1, the verse this card covers. The reference doesn't support the fact it is attached to.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The setup says James has 'something to say about how they treat people.' That rules out both wrong answers on card 2, because 'Argue about the law' and 'Brag about their giving' are not about how they treat people. Only 'Show favoritism' fits the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but 'Right by the door' and 'In the back row' are made-up seats. They are not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: No card ever tells what the poor man is told in James 2:3: 'You must stand' or 'Sit at my feet.' Card 5 only says he isn't offered a seat of honor. This is the heart of the favoritism picture, so the baker leaves without one of the passage's key details.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank in 'rich in ___' tests wording, not meaning. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason 'faith' over 'wisdom' or 'patience,' because all three fit the poor God has chosen. The baker can only guess the next word of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'beginner' and 'stranger' aren't believable outcomes of committing murder, so 'lawbreaker' stands out right away. It is also the only answer about breaking a law.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
